memories.commit_message: feat: add JWT authentication to Flask API
memories.reason: We needed stateless auth so the API could scale horizontally without shared session storage. JWT lets each worker verify tokens independently using a shared secret, with no database round-trip per request.

tradeoffs.chosen: Stateless JWTs — no server-side state, scales easily, no DB on every request
tradeoffs.rejected: Cookie sessions — require shared session store or sticky routing in multi-worker setup
tradeoffs.known_downsides: Cannot revoke tokens before expiry; if a token is compromised or a user must be locked out immediately, you have to wait up to 1 hour.

memories.commit_message: refactor: replace JWT with server-side sessions
memories.reason: A contractor account needed immediate lockout. Their JWT was still valid for ~45 minutes after we disabled the account. Server-side sessions can be cleared instantly server-side. The scalability argument for JWT turned out not to matter — we run two workers behind nginx and Flask's signed cookie session is fine.

tradeoffs.chosen: Server-side sessions — instant revocation, simpler logout, no library dependency
tradeoffs.rejected: Keeping JWT with a token blacklist — adds the same statefulness without simplifying the code
tradeoffs.known_downsides: Sessions are tied to a specific server unless we add a shared session store (Redis) later. Not suitable if we add mobile clients that can't use cookies.

memories.commit_message: perf: add Redis cache for /users list endpoint
memories.reason: During a Black Friday traffic spike the /users admin endpoint hit 380 ms p99. Profiling showed it was a three-table Postgres join that runs on every admin page load. Added a 60-second Redis cache in front of it; p99 dropped to 4 ms. TTL of 60 s was chosen because admin user lists are not time-sensitive — 1-minute stale data is acceptable.

tradeoffs.chosen: Redis cache with 60 s TTL — dramatic latency improvement, low complexity, reuses existing Redis
rejected: Postgres materialized view — harder to invalidate, requires DBA approval to add
Query optimization — tried adding an index, only reduced to 210 ms, not enough
tradeoffs.known_downsides: Up to 60 s of stale data for admin user list. Cache is not invalidated on writes yet (tracked as follow-up). Redis outage causes cache miss fallback to slow DB path.

memories.commit_message: security: add rate limiting to /login (credential-stuffing incident)
memories.reason: On 2024-11-08 we detected 14,000 login attempts in 3 minutes from a rotating IP pool — a credential-stuffing attack using a leaked password list. No accounts were breached but the auth service was saturated. Implemented per-IP rate limiting at 10 req/min on /login to make future attacks economically unviable.

tradeoffs.chosen: Flask-Limiter with Redis storage — ships in hours, logic lives in our codebase, no external dependency
rejected: WAF IP blocking — our plan tier requires a support ticket and 24-48 h turnaround
CAPTCHA on /login — adds friction for all users, including legitimate automated clients
tradeoffs.known_downsides: 10 req/min per IP can block legitimate users behind NAT/VPN sharing one IP. Sophisticated attackers with large IP pools can stay under per-IP limits. Does not address password reuse — recommend enforcing MFA separately.
